title: Basic Technology Year 9 Student Workbook
source: Ministry of Education, Fiji — Technical Employment Skills and Training, 2019
ai_role: Use this workbook as the primary Year 9 Basic Technology source when answering worksheet and drawing questions. Explain answers step-by-step and distinguish source-derived information from AI-generated guidance.
workflow: Identify the student's Year 9 topic or worksheet question.
Match the question to the relevant workbook lesson or sheet.
Explain the required technical-drawing method in simple steps.
If a student uploads a photograph, inspect the drawing, identify visible dimensions, instruments, line types, symbols and construction geometry, then solve the question.
Show the reasoning and final answer; do not invent dimensions that are not visible or stated.
If the image is unclear, ask the student to retake the photograph rather than guessing.
Where a drawing can be reconstructed, generate the corresponding CAD/technical-drawing construction.
Offer the matching workbook sheet as the learning source and save completed work to the e-Portfolio.
observed_workbook_topics: Pencil selection and technical drawing practice
Using set squares for vertical and angled lines
notes: Page 1 identifies the document as the Year 9 Basic Technology Student Workbook.
Page 2 states it was prepared for the Year 9 Basic Technology students section of the Technical Employment Skills and Training section of the Ministry of Education.
Page 3 covers basic drawing instruments including T-square, set squares, protractor, compass, divider and pencil.
Page 4 provides exercises using set squares to produce vertical and angled lines.
Pages 5–6 include centre-line and shape construction exercises.
Page 7 covers lettering, paper layout/title block and symbols/conventions.
Page 8 covers dimensioning practices and dimensioning of shapes.
